description:
RULED s394 (fable-answers-s393.md): these are blessed engine non-support, NOT Parser2-TODO-style gaps.  Three steps, in order:

1. perl-tests/t/test.pl stub: add capture_warnings (the real t/test.pl:1739 has it; the 46-sub stub does not).  This half of re/regex_sets.t is a HARNESS gap, fixable, and must not be buried under the engine registration.

2. re/script_run.t: XDIFF registration (docs/perl-suite-expected.tsv + expected-rows.tsv) citing a new docs/not-supported.md entry for (*script_run:...) / (+script_run:...): cl-ppcre has no script-run assertions.  Owner family #196/#71.  The entry MUST note PCRE2 has script_run (since 10.33), so #71 would LIFT this registration — blessed non-support of the current engine, not of PCL forever.

3. re/regex_sets.t: after step 1, re-measure, then register ONLY the (?[ ... ]) extended-character-class half.  Note: (?[ ]) is perl-only — not even PCRE2 implements it — so this half stays registered even under #71.

BAR: registration rows cite the not-supported entry; both files re-run and their snapshot rows spliced; the row counts stay visible as #196/#71 fix targets (XDIFF still runs and prints).

=== DONE s395d, all three steps.  (1) capture_warnings added to perl-tests/t/test.pl, verbatim from the real t/test.pl -- it had been an undef-fn crash that stopped re/regex_sets.t after 53 of 96 rows; the file now runs end to end at 4 ok / 84 not-ok.  (2)+(3) re/script_run.t and re/regex_sets.t registered XDIFF with new docs/not-supported.md sections, each stating whether task #71 (PCRE2) lifts it: script-run YES (PCRE2 has had it since 10.33), (?[ ]) NO (perl-only).  Rows blessed with --bless-rows; both files verified XDIFF afterwards.  NEW: task #323 -- warning_is/warning_like/warnings_like in that same stub PASS unconditionally (the #202 class), population measured.
